speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for Health with the low number of community cases for COVID-19, what can be expected on further easing of measures for Singapore and when can this be done.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Government has completed its review of work-from-home arrangements and where does Singapore stand in the Government's risk assessment in determining when to move into Phase 3 of Singapore's reopening.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Since then, we have progressed from Phase One to Phase Two.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have learned important lessons from other countries in easing precautionary measures for COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, when restrictions are lifted prematurely, or too hastily, a resurgence of cases may occur, resulting in the need to partially reimpose these restrictions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the other hand, it is not sustainable to maintain tight restrictions for a prolonged period which will severely impact not only our economy, but also our lives.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we have taken a carefully calibrated approach in opening up our society and economy as we work towards Phase Three.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is complemented by close monitoring, extensive testing and comprehensive contact tracing to keep the situation under control, as we balance the protection of lives and livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have made significant moves towards restoring economic and social activities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Work-related events, including conferences, seminars and meetings, have also been allowed to resume, albeit within a 50-person cap for these activities to reduce the risk of transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Other safe management measures should continue to be observed at workplaces.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have also taken steps to support the resumption of a few very targeted and specific areas.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Earlier, we had also allowed the resumption of physical exercise classes in common community spaces, and allowed an increase in capacity for cinemas and leisure attractions such as the Zoo and Bird Park.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are piloting live performances to prepare us to eventually be able to resume such activities safely.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Ms Jessica Tan has asked what can be expected on further easing of measures going forward and when this can be done; and I understand Ms Foo Mee Har1 would like to know whether the social and dining group size limit of five persons will be reviewed.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: All these are very important questions that we ask ourselves constantly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For instance, we could allow for general group sizes larger than five, so that larger families or groups of friends could meet and have meals together.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are particularly concerned about dining as we need to remove our masks so as to eat and drink, but we tend to also talk at the same time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The risk is considerably higher than activities which we can keep our masks on and maintain a safe distance.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have begun pilots of events and activities with a larger number of attendees, such as trade exhibitions, conferences and religious worship to assess whether we can maintain effective precautions and safe distancing measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If these pilots are successful, we will be able to use the lessons learnt to allow more large-scale events to proceed.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will also continue to facilitate further opening up for overseas travel in a safe and calibrated manner, which Minister Ong Ye Kung will talk about later in greater detail later.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The low number of community cases currently is not accidental but has come about due to our collective hard work and sacrifices.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even as we move towards Phase Three, the new normal will be different from what we were used to in the pre-COVID days.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As overseas travel restrictions are progressively eased and more activities resume, it has become even more critical that each of us plays our part to exercise social responsibility and adhere to the safe management measures, in order to keep our family and friends safe as we progress towards Phase Three.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I note that we are now at about 50% of our work-from-home policy, but I think Minister Lawrence Wong originally said that we should embrace working from home even after the circuit breaker ends.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, can I just check whether the Government still stands by that statement?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, I think working from home has allowed more fathers to play an active role in child care-giving duties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am just wondering whether the Government has studies or will be studying whether our work-from-home policies can contribute towards levelling the child care-giving duties at home and hence, tackling this gender stereotype?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Working from home will continue to be default, but we do accept and acknowledge that there are challenges both from the employers as well as from the employees' perspective.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is a flexible arrangement; we want to provide some flexibility for the workers and the employers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also recognise that some employers do need to consult their employees, they still need to have face-to-face interactions and meetings.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is also part of the process of team bonding and is critical among the employees.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We cannot totally do away with the face-to-face, physical meetings and interactions amongst employees and employers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we provide some flexibility but we still encourage employers and employees to work out the arrangements and to allow employees to stay at home, work from home, as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will help to reduce overcrowding in the workplaces and at the same time, also reduce the congestion on the roads and on public transport.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Through this period of COVID-19, we have found that working from home has a lot of advantages, like Mr Louis Ng has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: You can spend more time with your family and fathers can also play a bigger role in the family setting.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But this is a separate issue on family matters, which is probably more appropriate for the Member to file a separate Parliamentary Question (PQ) addressed to MSF, rather than for MOH to respond specifically.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But generally, we will continue to encourage working from home and we will continue to provide flexibility to allow flexible work arrangements between the employer and the employees.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: A reminder to Members to keep the supplementary questions relevant to the PQs, please.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Specific to the roadmap that Minister had mentioned that he would be sharing over the next couple weeks, may I ask, firstly, if there will be additional parameters or guidance given to businesses and individuals such that they will be able to make their planning in advance?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: For example, earlier, we allowed up to 50% of the employees to work from the office, but I think that was only given five days in advance of the 28 September date.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The other matter is in relation to my question on the Government's risk assessment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I thank him for the opportunity to explain and elaborate.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Because different sectors will have different challenges and we are working through these challenges with them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: You would have noticed that for some of the announcements, the notice period is very short, basically because there is really no need to meet any deadline.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, when you allow workers to go back to work – you can start on Monday, you can start next week, you can start next month.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is not a requirement that you must get them to go back to work and therefore, there is really no need for a lead time to prepare.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: You can take as long as you need to prepare yourselves, to discuss with your employees how to introduce this flexible arrangement.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, many of the measures, you would notice, we do not accumulate them into a big package and then announce them at once, so that there are many changes at one go.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We work with the sector leads to discuss how to help them, how to solve some of the challenges.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As and when these issues are addressed and solved, we move ahead.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some of them may not even require a specific public announcement because it may be very sector-specific and so we would just discuss with the sector.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When we come to some common understanding to make sure that safe management measures can be put in place, and we proceed with it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, these are differentiated approaches that we have adopted.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With regard to the DORSCON level, we have to always bear in mind that, as I have mentioned before, DORSCON level is not just determined by the number of cases alone.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I had mentioned in my reply, we will be opening up our borders.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will need to continue to encourage more travels because Singapore is a hub city.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we need to ensure that our travel hub and business hub status do not get undermined.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I should not go into too much detail on this because Minister Ong Ye Kung is all ready to speak on this.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I will leave it to him to elaborate.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we have to continue to maintain the DORSCON level and to keep our guards up, so that we can continue to keep the number of cases low, especially in the community.
